bottom_line: The fix pass mostly held up: of 37 verified findings (rank 8 has no verdict), 11 are fully fixed, 25 are partial, 1 is not_fixed, and there are no regressions and nothing that needs a runtime check â€” every verdict is code-evidenced at high confidence (only rank 11 is medium). The consistent pattern is that the visible/disclosure half of each fix landed while the deeper data-integrity or server-side half did not, so most partials are honest \"disclosed but not corrected\" states rather than failed work. Before the professor demo, prioritize the four high-severity data-integrity gaps that produce visibly wrong or fabricated numbers: rank 7 (invented 0.75-1.25 volume factor and synthetic LOS still exported into the formal report), rank 2 (\"S000001\" internal id leaking into user copy plus a disjoint third GEH pipeline), rank 24 (\"Best\" awarded on raw minimum totals, favoring scenarios that serve fewer vehicles), and rank 31 (average queue shown under a \"Max Q Length\" title) â€” any of these on screen or in the exported report would undermine credibility. Rank 18 (not_fixed) is the biggest UX gap: decision content is still buried at section 5 and intersection panels render empty on first load, so at minimum auto-seed a default intersection selection before the demo. The remaining partials (plain-mode jargon, backend-down contradictory panels, HTML-as-.doc export, number-format inconsistency, silent retries, missing upload cancel/timeout) are demo-safe to defer but should be tracked; the lone dead-code hazard (rank 38 SimulationControl) has no real importers and is not a demo risk.
